title: TensorPlate Platform Support Row
description: One exact platform support row: the unit the registry stores, `doctor` matches against, and release evidence is filed under. Every field is exact-version — a row names a specific OS version, driver/runtime stack, CPU architecture, accelerator SKU, and validation environment, and covers an explicit CPU vendor set, so evidence never transfers between rows. Non-exact future targets use the separate roadmap_target.json schema and are never rows. Memory accounting references the platform memory profile records by property name (`unified_memory` / `discrete_gpu`) rather than re-specifying them. This schema versions independently of the cross-process protocol; consumers reject other schema_version values as static-config errors. Free-text fields must also carry a non-whitespace character; that rule is enforced by consumers rather than by a `pattern`, because regex dialects disagree about which code points count as whitespace (U+FEFF and U+3000 among them) and a cross-language contract must not depend on that.

row_id.description: Stable identifier, unique across the registry. Lowercase alphanumeric segments joined by single hyphens so identifier resolution is unambiguous.

version.description: Exact OS version. Evidence from one version never satisfies another.

image_identity.description: Image or distribution identity where the OS version alone is not exact (e.g. a JetPack/L4T release on an Ubuntu base).

components.description: Kernel constraints and driver/runtime versions recorded exactly at evidence time (accelerator driver, compute runtime, inference runtime, Python, framework; or OS build plus framework on Apple rows). Planned rows declare an empty list until their first evidence run records the stack.

vendors.description: Host CPU vendors this row covers. A row with an accelerator names exactly one, because the accelerator SKU pins the host; an accelerator-less utility row may cover several. Drives `unsupported_cpu_vendor` by membership, with no out-of-band allowlist.

accelerator.description: Absent on accelerator-less rows. Names the exact SKU: a near-miss SKU never matches this row.

sku.description: Exact SKU as reported by the platform, recorded at first run.

memory_bytes.description: Accelerator memory size in bytes; must be positive. Integers in [0, 2^53) so a declared size can never be silently rounded by a JSON parser.

memory_profile.description: Reference to the platform memory profile record of the same property name; the profile owns budget domains, measurement sources, and headroom computation.

partitioning.description: Partition posture. `unsupported` means the platform can partition the accelerator but the row rejects partitioned devices fail-closed; `not_applicable` means the accelerator has no partitioning concept.

backend_packages.description: Required backend package set and package channel per backend path.

model_class_rows.description: Pointers to the model support rows valid on this platform row, with their support level. Empty where the row carries no model claim.

gate_semantics.description: Posture of every platform signal on this row. Every signal is declared; a signal that is absent on the row is recorded `not_applicable` with a reason rather than omitted.

support_level.description: Appliance-lifecycle support level. Planned rows commit their definition so later validation is a harness run, not re-planning; they carry no evidence and are excluded from supported combinations.

identity.description: Where the row's claim was validated, as prose: an exact machine type or physical device for a row scoped to one, or a statement of scope for a row whose claim is deliberately broader. Machine-comparable scoping lives in `machine_type`, not here.

machine_type.description: Exact machine-comparable shape identifier (e.g. a cloud machine type) for rows whose evidence is scoped to one. A row that declares this matches only a host reporting the same value, because evidence does not transfer across machine shapes. Omitted where the row's claim is not shape-scoped: physical rows are identified by their exact accelerator SKU, and accelerator-less utility rows make a deliberately chassis-independent claim. Must be a value a host probe can actually report, or the row can never match.

validation_environment.description: Exact machine type or physical device the row is validated on. `identity` is prose for humans; `machine_type` is the machine-comparable form used for matching.

evidence.description: Where install/upgrade logs, doctor output, smoke results, and telemetry samples for this row are filed. Required on Production rows, forbidden on Planned rows.

provenance.description: How this row definition was authored. `recorded` means the fields were transcribed from a real run on this exact hardware; `spec_authored` means they were authored from vendor specifications because no evidence run has been recorded for this row yet. Planned rows are always spec_authored and are re-verified against recorded output when their hardware first runs.

reason.description: Why the signal is not applicable on this row. Required for `not_applicable`; free-text row fact, not a typed platform reason.

allOf.$comment: A row without an accelerator cannot report GPU utilization.
An exact accelerator SKU pins the host, so such a row names one vendor.
